newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat in Egypt to consult on Washington summit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in Egypt to consult on Washington summit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Egypt on Monday for urgent consultations with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on whether Mubarak will go to U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East summit.

Arafat flew straight to the airport at the northwestern town of Burg al-Arab and began talks at Mubarak's country house nearby, officials said. Arafat is expected to fly to Cairo after the meeting, they added.

In Jerusalem, a PLO official said Arafat has asked Clinton to delay the summit, scheduled for Tuesday, until differences over the agenda are settled. The official said Arafat had not yet received a reply from Clinton.
Egyptian officials say Mubarak has not yet decided whether to go, unless someone can persuade him that Clinton and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have something to offer.
Palestinian officials say Arafat wants to go to Washington, provided Egypt sends a representative, possibly Foreign Minister Amr Moussa or presidential adviser Osama el-Baz.
Clinton called for the summit to help end five days of clashes in which 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis have died.
The clashes broke out after Israel opened a tunnel near the Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem, Islam's third-holiest site.

"The loss of life and the tragedy of the violence in the Middle East this week have been a terrible development for the Israeli and the Palestinian people, a blow to all those who have worked for a lasting peace, an encouragement to those who oppose a lasting peace," Clinton said.
But in an interview published on Monday, Mubarak said that unless Netanyahu carries out agreements signed by Israel and the Palestinian Authority, the violence could break out again.

"Even if things calm down now between the Israeli government and the Palestinians, no one can ensure the calm will continue. The situation can explode again, as long as the agreements and treaties are not implemented," he told the party newspaper Mayo.

"The latest events in the Palestinian territories are the natural result of procrastination in carrying out the articles of the agreements and the severe pressure on the economy of the Palestinian people," he added.
"I have warned before and I warn again of a new uprising by the Palestinians if they are in despair or lose hope that they will obtain their rights, as enshrined in charters.
"The new intifada will not be with stones, but with something more, and that's what we've seen pictures of in the last few days," he added.
Clinton, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, King Hussein of Jordan and Israeli President Ezer Weizman called Mubarak on Sunday to try to persuade him to go to Washington.
But Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told American television earlier that Egypt wanted to be sure the Washington summit would have clear goals and that Israel would abide by old agreements.

"We call on the U.S. to continue to ensure the peace process is back and this can't be ensured without a clear commitment by Netanyahu that he will heed all the agreements and implement all the documents," he said.
